facts: On a distance–time graph, the gradient of a straight segment is the constant speed during that stage.
A horizontal segment means the object is stopped, and that stopped time still counts in the total time.
The average speed for a whole journey is **not** the mean of the leg speeds.
For an out-and-back trip, add the distance both ways, because distance travelled is not net displacement.
Speed units are metres per second ($\text{m/s}$) or kilometres per hour ($\text{km/h}$).
steps: Find the total distance travelled over the journey from the graph or description.
Find the total time taken, including all stops and rest periods: $\Delta t = t_{\text{final}} - t_{\text{start}}$.
State the result with the correct speed units.

foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 60\text{ km}$
$\text{Total time} = 5\text{ h}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{60}{5}$
$= 12\text{ km/h}$

foundation.question_text: A distance–time graph has three stages: Stage A covers $40\text{ km}$ in $1\text{ h}$, Stage B covers $0\text{ km}$ in $0.5\text{ h}$, and Stage C covers $50\text{ km}$ in $2\text{ h}$. Identify which stage had the fastest travelling speed.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Speed in Stage A} = \dfrac{40}{1} = 40\text{ km/h}$
$\text{Speed in Stage B} = 0\text{ km/h}$
$\text{Speed in Stage C} = \dfrac{50}{2} = 25\text{ km/h}$
$\text{Stage A had the fastest travelling speed } (40\text{ km/h}).$

foundation.question_text: A runner accelerates smoothly such that distance in metres is given by $d(t) = 0.5t^2$ for $0 \le t \le 8\text{ s}$. Calculate the runner's average speed over the $8\text{-second}$ sprint.

A walker travels $1200\text{ m}$ in $15\text{ minutes}$, stops for $5\text{ minutes}$, and then walks another $600\text{ m}$ in $10\text{ minutes}$. Find their overall average speed in metres per minute.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 1200 + 600 = 1800\text{ m}$
$\text{Total time} = 15 + 5 + 10 = 30\text{ min}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{1800}{30}$
$= 60\text{ m/min}$

foundation.question_text: A driver travels $60\text{ km}$ at $60\text{ km/h}$ and then $120\text{ km}$ at $40\text{ km/h}$. Explain why the overall average speed is not $\frac{60+40}{2} = 50\text{ km/h}$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Time for leg 1} = \dfrac{60}{60} = 1\text{ h}$
$\text{Time for leg 2} = \dfrac{120}{40} = 3\text{ h}$
$\text{Total time} = 1 + 3 = 4\text{ h}$
$\text{Total distance} = 60 + 120 = 180\text{ km}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{180}{4} = 45\text{ km/h}$
$\text{The driver spends } 3\text{ hours at the slower speed and only } 1\text{ hour at the faster speed, so the speeds cannot be simply averaged.}$

foundation.question_text: A freight train travels $150\text{ km}$ in $2.5\text{ hours}$. Calculate its average speed in kilometres per hour.

development.question_text: A runner completes the first $10\text{ km}$ of a race in $50\text{ minutes}$ and the second $10\text{ km}$ in $70\text{ minutes}$. Calculate their average speed in $\text{km/h}$ for the entire $20\text{ km}$ race.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 20\text{ km}$
$\text{Total time} = 50 + 70 = 120\text{ min} = 2\text{ h}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{20}{2}$
$= 10\text{ km/h}$

development.question_text: An aircraft climbs such that its altitude in metres is $h(t) = 20t^2$ for $0 \le t \le 10\text{ s}$. Find its average vertical climb speed over the $10\text{-second}$ interval.

A student walks $3\text{ km}$ from home to the library in $45\text{ minutes}$, studies for $30\text{ minutes}$, and walks the $3\text{ km}$ back home in $45\text{ minutes}$. Find their average speed in $\text{km/h}$ for the entire outing.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 3 + 3 = 6\text{ km}$
$\text{Total time} = 45 + 30 + 45 = 120\text{ min} = 2\text{ h}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{6}{2}$
$= 3\text{ km/h}$

development.question_text: A drone flies $240\text{ m}$ in $12\text{ seconds}$, hovers stationary for $8\text{ seconds}$, and then flies another $360\text{ m}$ in $20\text{ seconds}$. Calculate its average speed across the $40\text{ seconds}$.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 240 + 360 = 600\text{ m}$
$\text{Total time} = 12 + 8 + 20 = 40\text{ s}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{600}{40}$
$= 15\text{ m/s}$

development.question_text: A motorist drives $90\text{ km}$ at $90\text{ km/h}$ and $90\text{ km}$ at $60\text{ km/h}$. Calculate the overall average speed and determine whether it is closer to $60\text{ km/h}$ or $90\text{ km/h}$.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Time 1} = \dfrac{90}{90} = 1\text{ h}$
$\text{Time 2} = \dfrac{90}{60} = 1.5\text{ h}$
$\text{Total time} = 1 + 1.5 = 2.5\text{ h}$
$\text{Total distance} = 90 + 90 = 180\text{ km}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{180}{2.5} = 72\text{ km/h}$
$\text{The average speed is } 72\text{ km/h, which is closer to } 60\text{ km/h because more time was spent at the slower speed.}$

mastery.question_text: A commuter travels a distance of $d\text{ km}$ to work at $40\text{ km/h}$ and returns the same distance $d\text{ km}$ along the same route at $60\text{ km/h}$. Show that the overall average speed is $48\text{ km/h}$, independent of $d$.

A courier drove a total of $210\text{ km}$ in $3.5\text{ hours}$. They travelled at $80\text{ km/h}$ on the motorway for $t$ hours and $40\text{ km/h}$ in city traffic for the remainder of the time. Find $t$ and the distance travelled on the motorway.

An object moves along a straight line with position $s(t) = t^3 - 2t^2 + 5t$ metres over the time interval $0 \le t \le 4\text{ s}$. Find its average speed and show that it equals the gradient of the chord connecting $(0, s(0))$ and $(4, s(4))$.
mastery.solution_text:
$s(0) = 0\text{ m}$
$s(4) = 4^3 - 2(4^2) + 5(4) = 64 - 32 + 20 = 52\text{ m}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{52 - 0}{4 - 0} = 13\text{ m/s}$
$\text{Chord gradient} = \dfrac{s(4) - s(0)}{4 - 0} = \dfrac{52 - 0}{4} = 13\text{ m/s}$
$\text{The average speed is exactly equal to the gradient of the chord, } 13\text{ m/s}.$
